Excursions from Fez

Day trips with a driver-guide. We pick you up at your accommodation.

Meknes and Volubilis

Meknes, at the foot of the Middle Atlas, is the most modest of the four imperial cities. We visit its medina, stroll through its souks and see el-Hedim square, the heart of the city, the Bab el-Mansour gate, the Bou Inania madrasa and the mausoleum of Moulay Ismail, among the many corners of this beautiful imperial city. We round off the day with the Roman ruins of Volubilis.

Book

Ifrane and Azrou

Ifrane, known as "Little Switzerland", lies in the Atlas mountains: clean and orderly, it is a typical winter destination for ski lovers. We see the outside of the royal palace, Al Akhawayn University, the centre with its terraces and the stone lion carved by a German soldier. Azrou, a Berber town 80 km from Fez, is surrounded by the famous forests of ancient cedars, home to Barbary macaques.

Book

Moulay Idriss

70 km from Fez, one of the most famous pilgrimage sites in Morocco. Because of its religious status it was closed to non-Muslims until the 20th century. It is the sanctuary of the founder of the Idrisid dynasty, Idris I, considered a descendant of the Prophet. We visit the mausoleum, the square, the round minaret and the panoramic terraces overlooking the whole town.
